title: Exam Orientation and the Command-Line Toolkit

header.html: exam environment and speed kit (supports every competency)
Kubernetes v1.37.0 (3-node test cluster, containerd 2.3.4, etcd 3.7.0)

toc.title: JSONPath and custom columns (a frequent time-saver)
A repeatable way to work every task

html:
1What the exam is

The exam is performance-based. You get a live terminal, not multiple-choice questions. You solve real tasks on real clusters, and a script scores the final cluster state, not the commands you typed.

Item Value (official pages, fetched 2026-11-09)
Format 15 to 20 performance-based tasks in a live terminal, online proctored
Duration 2 hours
Kubernetes version v1.37
Passing score 66%
Price USD 445, exam only; includes one retake
Validity 2 years
Simulator killer.sh, 2 attempts of 36 hours each, included with registration
Results Emailed within 24 hours

Not published on the pages used for this course: how many clusters you will switch between and the exact points per task. Do not rely on a number from a blog. Read the context line of every task.

Domain weights

Domain Weight Where it is taught
Troubleshooting 30% Modules 11 to 13, plus a break-and-fix task in every module
Cluster Architecture, Installation and Configuration 25% Modules 1 to 4
Services and Networking 20% Modules 7 to 9
Workloads and Scheduling 15% Modules 5 and 6
Storage 10% Module 10

Exam focus: time goes where points are. Troubleshooting plus Architecture is 55% of the score.

2The exam environment

  • You start on a host called base. Tasks name the host to use, and you reach it with ssh <node>. You cannot SSH from one node to another (no nested SSH). Type exit to return to base. Use sudo -i to become root on a node.
  • Every task begins with a context line, usually a kubectl config use-context ... command. Run it first. Working in the wrong cluster scores zero.
  • kubectl is installed with the alias k and shell autocompletion. Also installed: yq, curl, wget, man.
  • The Insert key is prohibited. Do not reboot base.
  • Allowed documentation: kubernetes.io/docs and the Kubernetes blog, helm.sh/docs, gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io (CKA only), the Quick Reference links in the exam, and distribution documents under /usr/share. The kubernetes.io search is allowed. Do not open external search results.

In this course's lab cluster there is no ssh. A small wrapper turns ssh cka-worker 'command' into docker exec. Everything else (kubectl, files, manifests) behaves as on the exam. Files you are asked to save go to ~/answers/ on the machine where you run kubectl.

3The speed kit

Typing YAML by hand is slow. Generate it, then edit.

export do="--dry-run=client -o yaml"      # then:  k run web --image=nginx:alpine $do > pod.yaml
export now="--force --grace-period 0"     # then:  k delete pod web $now
alias kn='kubectl config set-context --current --namespace'
Need Command
Pod k run web --image=nginx:alpine --labels=tier=web
Deployment k create deployment api --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=3
Service for something that exists k expose deployment api --port=80
Any object as a template add --dry-run=client -o yaml
Find a field name k explain pod.spec.containers --recursive or k explain pod.spec | grep -i grace
List with more columns k get pods -o wide
One value k get node n1 -o jsonpath='{.status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion}'
Loop over items -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}'
Chosen columns -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,IMG:.spec.containers[0].image
Sort --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
Default namespace k config set-context --current --namespace=speed
Can this user do it? k auth can-i get pods --as jane -n dev

Editor: vim is the safe choice. Put set expandtab tabstop=2 shiftwidth=2 in ~/.vimrc so pasted YAML keeps its indentation.

kubectl explain beats searching. It shows the exact field names for the cluster version you are on, with no browser and no tab-switching. Use --recursive for the whole tree.

Read the whole task before typing. The scoring script checks every sentence of the task. A missing label or the wrong namespace costs the full task.

Imperative first, declarative when needed

Imperative commands (run, create, expose, set, scale, label) are fastest for simple objects. When a field has no flag, generate YAML with --dry-run=client -o yaml, edit it, and apply -f. For a running object, k edit changes it in place.

3b. Labels and selectors (they connect everything)

Labels are key/value tags on objects; Services, Deployments, NetworkPolicies, affinity rules and kubectl filters all find objects by label.

k get pods --show-labels
k get pods -l env=prod                     # equality selector
k get pods -l 'env in (prod,dev),tier!=db' # set-based selector
k label pod p1 env=prod --overwrite        # add or change a label (--overwrite to change)
k label pod p1 env-                        # remove the label (trailing minus)
k delete pods -l env=dev                   # act on every match
k annotate pod p1 note="checked"           # annotations: free-form metadata, not selectable

A Service or Deployment selector that does not match the Pod template labels is a classic exam fault (Modules 7 and 13).

4JSONPath and custom columns (a frequent time-saver)

jsonpath pulls exact values out of an object, which is how tasks such as "write the names of all nodes to a file" are solved:

k get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}' | sort > nodes.txt
  • {.items[*].metadata.name} prints names on one line separated by spaces.
  • range ... end plus {"\n"} puts one per line.
  • -o name prints node/<name>; if the task wants the bare name, use jsonpath or sed.
  • custom-columns prints a header unless you remove it (--no-headers); check the task for "without header".

5A repeatable way to work every task

  1. Read the task and the context line; run the use-context command.
  2. Note the namespace and the names given. Use them exactly.
  3. Do the task with the fastest command.
  4. Verify with one command (k get, k describe, k logs, curl). A task that "should" work and does not is the most common loss.
  5. If a task is stuck after about 6 minutes, flag it, move on, and return at the end.

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m00 -->

Lab 0.1: jsonpath nodes

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 3 | Time: about 3 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m00-01-jsonpath-nodes)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Save the names of all nodes, one name per line, sorted alphabetically and without a header line, to ~/answers/nodes.txt on the host where you run kubectl (the exam's base host).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}' | sort > ~/answers/nodes.txt
cat ~/answers/nodes.txt

Lab 0.2: dry run yaml

Domain: Workloads | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m00-02-dry-run-yaml)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Create the namespace speed. Generate (do not hand-write) a Pod manifest for a Pod named probe with image nginx:alpine and the label tier=web, and save it to ~/answers/pod.yaml. Then create the Pod from that file in the namespace speed.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl create ns speed
kubectl -n speed run probe --image=nginx:alpine --labels=tier=web --dry-run=client -o yaml > ~/answers/pod.yaml
kubectl apply -f ~/answers/pod.yaml -n speed
kubectl -n speed wait --for=condition=Ready pod/probe --timeout=120s

Lab 0.3: explain field

Domain: Workloads | Points: 3 | Time: about 3 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m00-03-explain-field)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Without opening a browser, use kubectl explain to find the name of the Pod spec field that sets how many seconds a Pod gets to shut down gracefully after it is told to stop. Write only the field name to ~/answers/field.txt.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl explain pod.spec | grep -i grace
echo terminationGracePeriodSeconds > ~/answers/field.txt

Lab 0.4: default namespace

Domain: Workloads | Points: 3 | Time: about 3 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m00-04-default-namespace)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Create the namespace speed. Change the current context so that kubectl uses speed as its default namespace, without editing any file by hand and without changing the context name.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl create ns speed
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=speed

Lab 0.5: labels selectors

Domain: Workloads | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m00-05-labels-selectors)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace lbl, three Pods exist: p1, p2 and p3, each with the label env=dev. Change the label env of p1 and p2 to prod (do not recreate them). Write the names of all Pods with env=prod, one per line and sorted, to ~/answers/prod.txt on the host, using a label selector. Then delete all Pods that still have env=dev using a label selector (not by name).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n lbl label pod p1 p2 env=prod --overwrite
kubectl -n lbl get pods --show-labels
kubectl -n lbl get pods -l env=prod -o name | sed 's#pod/##' | sort > ~/answers/prod.txt
kubectl -n lbl delete pods -l env=dev

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1What does the exam score: the commands you typed or the final cluster state?

Show the answer

The final cluster state.

R2What is the first action on every task?

Show the answer

Run the context line (the kubectl config use-context command) given in the task.

R3Which domain carries the highest weight, and what is the weight?

Show the answer

Troubleshooting, 30%.

R4What is the passing score and how long is the exam?

Show the answer

66% and 2 hours.

R5How do you reach another host on the exam, and can you SSH from one node to another?

Show the answer

With ssh <node> from base; nested SSH is not allowed, so type exit first.

R6Which command shows the exact name of a Pod spec field for the cluster you are on?

Show the answer

kubectl explain pod.spec (add --recursive for the whole tree).

R7How do you generate a Pod manifest without creating the Pod?

Show the answer

Add --dry-run=client -o yaml to kubectl run.

R8Which websites may you open during the exam?

Show the answer

kubernetes.io docs and blog, helm.sh/docs, gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io, and the Quick Reference links in the exam; not external search results.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Score 66% to pass; 2 hours; 15 to 20 tasks; state is scored
Weights Troubleshooting 30, Architecture 25, Networking 20, Workloads 15, Storage 10
Start of every task use-context, namespace, exact names
Generate YAML --dry-run=client -o yaml
Find fields kubectl explain ... [--recursive]
Output control -o jsonpath, -o custom-columns, --sort-by, -o wide
Hosts ssh <node>, sudo -i, exit; no nested SSH
Stuck for 6 minutes flag it, move on
